title: The Plural, and the Predicate
summary: One letter, -j, makes the plural of nouns and of the adjectives that go with them; the article and the verb stay as they are. A noun or adjective joined to the subject by *estas* is a predicate, and agrees in number with what it is predicated of.

rules.heading: The Plural Number
rules.statement: The **plural** of a noun — the form indicating more than one person or thing — is made by adding **-j** to the singular. The -o remains, so that the plural ending is in effect **-oj**, pronounced as the diphthong *oj* (¶5) and forming no new syllable.
footnotes: -oj is one syllable and sounds like the "oy" of "boy", so *viroj* is VI-roj, of two syllables, and the accent stays where it was.

rules.heading: Agreement of the Adjective in Number
rules.statement: An adjective modifying a plural noun **agrees with it in number**, taking the same -j. An adjective modifying two or more nouns together is of course plural. The agreement is not decoration: it is what tells the reader which noun a given adjective belongs to when the order of words is varied.

examples.note: one adjective, two nouns, hence the plural

footnotes: -aj is one syllable and sounds like the "ai" of "aisle".

rules.heading: The Article and the Verb are Invariable
rules.statement: The article **does not change** for number: *la viro*, the man; *la viroj*, the men. Neither does the verb, whose -as serves every person and both numbers alike (¶14). In a plural sentence, therefore, the -j appears on the noun and its adjectives and nowhere else.

examples.gloss: The men walk, the men are walking.

examples.target: La suno kaj la luno brilas.
examples.gloss: The sun and the moon are shining.

examples.target: La viro estas. / La viroj estas.
examples.gloss: The man is. / The men are.

rules.heading: The Predicate Adjective
rules.statement: When an adjective forms part of what is told or **predicated** of the subject — as after the verbs "to be", "to seem" — it is called a **predicate adjective**. It is not attached to its noun but asserted of it, and the verb stands between them.

rules.heading: The Predicate Noun
rules.statement: A **noun** may likewise form part of the predicate, and is then called a **predicate noun**. It names the subject rather than being acted upon by it, which is why it takes no case ending of its own.

rules.heading: Agreement of the Predicate
rules.statement: Predicate nouns and adjectives **agree in number** with the word or words of which they are predicated. Two singular subjects joined by *kaj* are together plural, and take a plural predicate.

examples.target: La knabo kaj la viro ŝajnas fortaj.
examples.gloss: The boy and the man seem strong.

vocabulary.notes: Perfectly regular: one form for every person and both numbers.

drills.explanation: -j is added to the singular, giving -oj. Nothing is dropped and no syllable is added: TA-bloj.
The adjective agrees in number, so both words take -j. *bonoj* would be a plural noun.

drills.stem: How does the article change before a plural noun?
options: It does not change: la viroj.
drills.explanation: *la* is invariable. In a plural sentence the -j appears on the noun and its adjectives, and nowhere else.

options: La arboj estas altaj kaj verdaj.
drills.explanation: A predicate adjective agrees in number with what it is predicated of, so *bela* must be *belaj*. The verb never takes -j: *estasj* is impossible.

drills.stem: In **La kolombo estas birdo**, what is *birdo*?
drills.explanation: It is a noun forming part of what is asserted of the subject *kolombo* — a predicate noun. It names the subject rather than being acted upon by it.

drills.stem: Translate: **The boy and the man seem strong.**
options: La knabo kaj la viro ŝajnas forta.
La knabo kaj la viro ŝajnas fortaj.
La knaboj kaj la viroj ŝajnas forta.
La knabo kaj la viro ŝajnasj fortaj.
drills.explanation: Two singular subjects joined by *kaj* are together plural, so the predicate adjective takes -j — but the subjects themselves stay singular, and the verb never changes.

drills.stem: In **La grandaj ĉevaloj kuras en la verdaj kampoj**, which words carry the plural -j?
drills.explanation: Adjectives and nouns take -j; the verb and the article never do.

drills.stem: In **Freŝaj floroj kuŝas sur la longa tablo**, how many words carry the plural ending **-j**?
drills.explanation: Two: *freŝaj* and *floroj*. The table is singular, so *longa* and *tablo* keep the singular; *kuŝas*, *sur* and *la* can never take -j at all.

drills.stem: How many syllables are there in **viroj**?
drills.explanation: Two: VI-roj. The plural ending -oj is the diphthong *oj* and counts as a single syllable, so making a noun plural never moves the accent.

drills.title: En la ĝardeno
drills.passage: La alta viro estas en la ĝardeno. Blanka ĉevalo estas en la kampo. Belaj birdoj sidas sur la verda arbo. La ĉambroj en la bela domo estas grandaj. Freŝaj floroj kuŝas sur la tablo. La kolomboj estas belaj birdoj. La arboj estas altaj kaj verdaj. Ruĝaj kaj flavaj folioj estas en la ĝardeno.
drills.translation: The tall man is in the garden. A white horse is in the field. Beautiful birds are sitting on the green tree. The rooms in the beautiful house are large. Fresh flowers are lying on the table. The doves are beautiful birds. The trees are tall and green. Red and yellow leaves are in the garden.

questions.stem: Kie estas la blanka ĉevalo? (Where is the white horse?)
questions.explanation: *Blanka ĉevalo estas en la kampo.* It is the tall man who is in the garden.

questions.stem: Which of these does the passage assert?
options: Freŝaj floroj kuŝas sur la tablo.
questions.explanation: The doves are called *belaj birdoj*, not flowers. Note that every predicate here is plural, agreeing with a plural subject.

questions.stem: How many **plural nouns** appear in the passage?
questions.explanation: Seven: birdoj, ĉambroj, floroj, kolomboj, birdoj (a second time, in the predicate), arboj, folioj. Every one is recognisable by -oj, and each is accompanied by adjectives in -aj.
